what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows computation directly on encrypted data without decrypting it, which is valuable for running AI models privately on sensitive information. Existing FHE accelerators for deep learning are built as single-node chips with many parallel compute blocks stacked together, which cannot exploit parallelism across the layers of a neural network and cannot scale beyond one card as models grow larger. Hydra takes a different approach: it spreads a deep learning model across multiple server nodes, each implemented on an FPGA (a field-programmable gate array — a chip whose internal wiring can be reconfigured by software rather than being fixed at manufacture), where each node handles a portion of the model's layers. A central scheduling process on the host server coordinates data routing between nodes so the encrypted computations flow as a pipeline through the cluster. This design is meant to scale to any number of nodes, removing the single-card bottleneck.
